title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant in the FMCG sector based in Bristol, you'll play a key role in managing financial records and ensuring smooth day-to-day operations. This role supports the accounting team by handling transactions, maintaining accurate records, and contributing to the overall financial health of the business.

Client Details

This opportunity is with a company operating in the FMCG sector, based in Bristol.

Description
- Process invoices, payments, and expense claims accurately and in a timely manner.
- Reconcile bank statements and resolve discrepancies as needed.
- Assist in preparing financial reports and maintaining records.
- Support month-end and year-end financial processes.
- Maintain accounts payable and receivable ledgers.
- Liaise with suppliers and customers to resolve payment queries.
- Provide general administrative support to the accounting team.
- Ensure compliance with financial policies and procedures.

Profile

A successful Accounts Assistant should have:
- Experience in accounting or finance, ideally within the FMCG industry.
- Knowledge of accounting software and proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- An understanding of financial processes and procedures.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a willingness to learn.

Job Offer
- Competitive salary ranging from £25,000 to £27,000 per year, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position in the FMCG industry in Bristol.
- Opportunity to develop your skills in a supportive accounting and finance team.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

People are at the heart of Michael Page. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment. As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Administrator - Financial Services
description:
We are working with a highly successful and rapidly growing financial services business to recruit an additional Financial Services Administrator to join their Bristol team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator with a background in financial services, particularly those with experience across pensions, investments, platforms, providers or financial products, who are looking to develop their career within a successful and expanding organisation.

The business has experienced significant growth in recent years and has ambitious plans for further expansion. Despite its growing national presence, it maintains a strong focus on local teams, collaboration and delivering an excellent experience for clients.

The Role

The successful candidate will join a small, supportive administration team and work closely with Advisers, Paraplanners and colleagues across the wider business.

The role will provide broad exposure to financial services administration, supporting the processing of client business and ongoing servicing requirements. Responsibilities will include:
- Processing financial services administration across pensions, investments and other financial products
- Using provider and platform systems to process transactions and client instructions
- Processing new business and top-up applications
- Processing fund switches, purchases, sales and income withdrawal requests
- Processing Letters of Authority and obtaining information from providers
- Supporting advisers with client meeting preparation and collating relevant information
- Preparing client reports, review packs and supporting documentation
- Maintaining accurate client records and updating internal systems
- Supporting ongoing client servicing and administration
- Assisting with wider administrative projects and supporting colleagues during busy periods

About You

This role is particularly suited to someone with previous financial services administration experience, rather than requiring a specific background within IFA or financial planning.

Relevant experience could include working within pensions, investments, wealth management, platforms, insurance, banking or other areas of financial services.

Strong administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage and prioritise your workload are essential. You will also need to be confident communicating with clients, providers and colleagues and be comfortable learning new systems and processes.

Package
- Salary up to £35,000
- Hybrid working - minimum 2 day a week in the office
- Strong holiday entitlement + birthday off
- Opportunity to purchase additional annual leave
- Good pension contributions
- Private medical insurance
- Life assurance x 4
- Income protection
- Full support with professional exams and relevant training
- A number of additional company benefits

The Opportunity

This is a great opportunity for a Financial Services Administrator looking to join a growing organisation where they can build on their existing industry experience, develop new skills and establish a long-term career.

The role offers the opportunity to gain wider exposure across financial services while working within a supportive team and benefiting from the resources, career opportunities and stability of a growing national business.

title: Claims Handler
description:
Job Title: Claims Handler

Location: Bristol (Hybrid - 3 days per week in the office)

Salary: Up to £35,000

Benefits: Hybrid working, professional qualification support (CII), long-term progression opportunities

About the Company:

This is an opportunity to join a well-established and growing specialist insurer with a strong reputation across financial lines, construction, accident & health, and affinity products. Backed by a major international parent group, the business combines the stability and support of a global insurer with the close-knit culture of a smaller regional team. With excellent staff retention and ambitious growth plans over the next few years, the business offers genuine long-term career development within a collaborative environment.

Role Summary:

This is an opportunity to join a busy claims function and manage insurance claims from first notification through to settlement or resolution.

You'll take ownership of claim outcomes, work closely with customers, brokers, adjusters and suppliers, and build broader technical exposure across coverage, liability, reserving and claims decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:
- Manage claims from FNOL through to resolution: Build end-to-end claims experience while taking ownership of outcomes
- Review policy terms, coverage and claim documentation: Develop stronger technical judgement around coverage and liability decisions
- Communicate with customers and brokers: Build trusted relationships while providing clear and professional claims updates
- Liaise with TPAs, adjusters and suppliers: Gain exposure to the wider claims process and external stakeholders
- Maintain accurate, audit-ready claim files: Strengthen your understanding of regulatory, data and compliance requirements
- Monitor reserves, indemnity spend and settlement strategy: Develop commercial awareness and intelligent claims decision-making

Requirements:
- Experience or technical knowledge of insurance claims, including the claims lifecycle from FNOL through to settlement
- Understanding of policy wordings, coverage principles and liability assessment, with familiarity with Civil Procedure Rules and the litigation process
- Awareness of FCA requirements, Consumer Duty, data protection and fair customer outcomes
- Confident communication, organisation and claims-system skills, with the ability to manage workloads and escalate complex matters appropriately

If this role isn't quite right, it's still worth speaking to one of our specialist team - we may be working on something that hasn't hit the market yet.

Related Job Titles: Claims Advisor, Claims Technician, Claims Adjuster, Claims Specialist, Insurance Claims Handler

title: Claims Handler
description:
Reed is recruiting for a number of Claims Handler opportunities with a leading Bristol-based organisation in the insurance sector, conveniently located just a short walk from Temple Meads.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong customer service skills who enjoys helping people, is confident communicating over the phone and is looking to build a long-term career within the insurance industry. Previous insurance experience is not required, and we welcome applications from a wide range of backgrounds including customer service, retail, hospitality, contact centres, complaints handling, banking, financial services and administration.

Working Hours: Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm (35 hours per week).

Hybrid Working: Office-based during training, with hybrid working introduced as confidence develops within the role.

Assessment Centre Dates
- Thursday 1st October, 9:00am-1:00pm
- Monday 5th October, 1:00pm-4:00pm

Start Date
- Monday 9th November

Full preparation and guidance will be provided ahead of the assessment centre.

The Role

As a Claims Handler, you'll manage legal expenses insurance claims from first notification through to conclusion. You'll investigate claims, review policy cover, assess information and evidence, communicate decisions and support customers throughout the claims journey.

This is a telephone-focused role, with much of your day spent speaking with customers. You'll be handling a mixture of routine enquiries and more challenging conversations, making empathy, resilience and strong communication skills essential.

About You

We're looking for people who can demonstrate:
- Previous customer service experience
- A confident and professional telephone manner
- Strong communication skills
- Empathy and resilience
- Attention to detail
- Good problem-solving ability
- A genuine desire to learn and develop a long-term career within insurance

Training & Progression

A comprehensive training programme is provided, including an initial two weeks of classroom-based learning followed by structured 10 weeks of coaching and support. This organisation is known for developing its people and offers clear progression opportunities into senior, technical and leadership positions, making it an excellent opportunity for someone looking to establish a successful career in the insurance sector.

Benefits
- £27,000 starting salary
- 35-hour working week
- Hybrid working following training
- 26 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
- Additional "My Day" leave entitlement
- Option to buy additional holiday
- Pension matched up to 10%
- Health Cash Plan
- Excellent career progression opportunities

Recruitment Process

Successful applicants will attend an assessment centre consisting of a competency-based interview, claims assessment exercise and telephone role play. Offers will be made shortly afterwards for either the November or January intake.

If you're looking to build a long-term career within the insurance industry and want to join an organisation that invests heavily in training, development and progression, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Communications Officer
description:
Role: Communications Officer

Sector: Public Sector

Duration: Interim 6 Months

Location: Bristol

Salary: £23.50 PAYE per hour

Sellick Partnership is currently recruiting for an experienced Officer to join our client based in Bristol. This role is offered on a full time, hybrid role with a minimum of 3 days a week in the office.

The Communications Officer will be responsible for developing and maintaining strong stakeholder relationships, supporting senior leadership engagement, monitoring external developments, and ensuring insights are effectively shared across the organisation.

The duties of the Communications Officer will include;
- Leading the coordination and delivery of a programme of stakeholder engagement activity, including senior leadership visits and meetings
- Supporting the planning and delivery of online and in-person events for senior external audiences Building and maintaining productive relationships with a wide range of external organisations and stakeholders
- Producing high-quality briefings for senior leaders ahead of meetings, events and stakeholder engagements
- Monitoring parliamentary and policy developments, providing concise summaries and insight to internal colleagues
- Supporting the preparation of evidence, briefing materials and background information for senior leaders
- Developing and improving systems and processes for managing stakeholder intelligence and engagement activity
- Creating engaging internal and external communications, including blogs, briefings and updates.
- Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives across the wider team

The Communications Officer will ideally have:
- Previous experience in a similar role
- Previous experience within the public sector
- Experience preparing briefings, reports, correspondence or communications for senior audiences.
- Strong organisational and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across teams and functions

The Communications and Engagement Specialist will need to have excellent communication skills and effectively be able to communicate to stakeholders of all levels. Furthermore, the ideal candidate will have an impeccable eye for detail and accuracy to ensure all workload is carried out effectively and efficiently. They will also need to able to prioritise their workload and be efficient and effective to meet unpredictable deadlines and deal with conflicting demands, whilst working in a high-pressured environment.

Our client is hoping to have the Communications Officer in the role as soon as possible, therefore if you believe your experience meets the criteria above, please contact Charlotte Broomfield by Monday 7 September by 5pm by submitted your CV directly.

Sellick Partnership is proud to be an inclusive and accessible recruitment business and we support applications from candidates of all backgrounds and circumstances. Please note, our advertisements use years' experience, hourly rates, and salary levels purely as a guide and we assess applications based on the experience and skills evidenced on the CV. For information on how your personal details may be used by Sellick Partnership, please review our data processing notice on our website.

title: IT Co-ordinator
description:
We have an exciting opportunity to join our IT here at Framatome UK!

Energise Your Career with Framatome UK - Powering a Safer, Smarter Nuclear Future

We are currently seeking a IT Co-ordinator to join our team in Avonmouth to support with the successful planning, governance, delivery and continuous improvement of IT projects and initiatives.

Working across business and technology teams, the IT Co-ordinator ensures projects are delivered efficiently, transparently and in line with business objectives and IT strategy.

What will you be doing?

Project Coordination & Delivery
- Coordinating the planning, execution, and monitoring of IT projects and work streams
- Support Project Managers and IT leadership in managing project schedules, milestones, deliverables and dependencies
- Tracking project progress and ensure timely completion of agreed actions
- Maintain project documentation, including project plans, RAID logs, status reports and governance artefacts
- Facilitating project meetings, workshops, and steering committees, documenting actions and decisions
- Monitoring project risks, issues and changes, escalating where needed
- Supporting resource planning and capacity management activities across the IT portfolio

Delivery Framework & Governance
- Champion adherence to IT project delivery methodologies, governance and best practice
- Ensuring projects comply with established delivery frameworks, stage gates and approval processes
- Maintaining governance documentation, templates, reporting standards and project controls
- Supporting portfolio reporting by consolidating project status updates, KPIs, milestones and delivery metrics
- Driving continuous improvement of project management processes and delivery governance
- Assisting in the development and implementation of PMO and project governance frameworks
- Supporting audit, compliance and regulatory requirements relating to project delivery activities

Stakeholder Management
- Building strong working relationships with different stakeholders
- Central point of coordination between project teams, users, vendors, and leadership
- Informing stakeholders of progress, risks, issues, and decisions
- Facilitating effective communication across departments and organisational levels
- Support stakeholder engagement activities, including requirements gathering, impact assessments and change planning
- Managing meetings schedules and communication plans

Vendor & Third-Party Coordination
- Coordinating activities with technology vendors and external service providers
- Monitoring supplier deliverables against agreed timelines and requirements
- Supporting contract, service review and performance tracking activities where required
- Escalating supplier issues and risks to project and IT leadership teams

Reporting & Administration
- Producing regular project status reports and executive summaries
- Maintaining project repositories and document management systems
- Ensuring accuracy and completeness of project records and governance documentation
- Supporting budget tracking, purchase requests and project financial reporting where required
- Providing administrative support to project boards and governance forums

What are we looking for?

Essential
- Experience coordinating IT projects, programmes, or technology initiatives and supporting project governance and delivery frameworks
- Strong understanding of project management methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, Hybrid)
- Excellent stakeholder management
- Communication skills
- Strong organisational and planning abilities
- Attention to detail
- Experience managing risks, issues, actions, and dependencies
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft 365 applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint
- Prioritise in a fast-paced environment

Desirable
- Experience within a PMO or IT delivery function
- Knowledge of ITIL practices and service management processes
- Experience using project management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Monday. com, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project or COEDM3
- Professional certifications such as:
- PRINCE2 Foundation/Practitioner
- Agile Foundation or Scrum certification
- PMQ, PMP, or equivalent
- ITIL Foundation

Key Competencies
- Project Coordination
- Stakeholder Management
- Governance & Compliance
- Planning & Organisation
- Communication & Influencing
- Risk & Issue Management
- Continuous Improvement
- Collaboration & Teamwork
- Problem Solving
- Attention to Detail

Work pattern: Hybrid

Benefits we offer:
- 25 daysannual leave per year rising by 1 day for every 2 years worked (max 30 days) + Bank Holidays
- 8% employer pension contribution with employee 1% contribution (salary sacrifice)
- Employee assistance programme (EAP)

Our benefits package also includes Individual and family private health care, Dental insurance - individual cover, Cashplan - Level 2 cover - individual and family cover, Life assurance (4x salary), Income Protection, Professional Body Membership, Tusker Electric car scheme (salary sacrifice), Cycle to Work scheme (salary sacrifice), Babbel - learn a new language and Generous family leave.

At Framatome we are a global leader in nuclear energy, recognised for delivering innovative, value-added technologies that design, build, maintain, and advance the world's nuclear fleet. With 22,000 employees in over 70 locations worldwide, we provide components, fuel, and control systems for nuclear power plants, along with a full suite of reactor services - all focused on improving safety, performance, and sustainability.

Backed by EDF Group (80.5%) and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (19.5%), we're driving the future of clean energy. Here in the UK, our team is now over 500 strong - and growing. As we expand our service offerings across the UK nuclear industry, we're aiming continuing our growth journey.

Now's your chance to join a company that's shaping the energy transition - where your expertise will matter, your growth will be supported, and your work will help power generations to come.

Apply Now!

title: Sales and Partnerships Coordinator
company: Not For Profit People - Agency - Permanent
description:
Sales and Partnerships Coordinator

We are seeking a proactive Sales and Partnerships Coordinator to generate new opportunities, build relationships and grow demand for consultancy and training services.

Salary: £30,559 to £32,654 FTE
Hours: 22.5 hours per week, flexibly across three or more days
Location: Bristol, with flexible/remote working and some office attendance required
Contract: Permanent
Closing date: Midday, Monday 5 October 2026
Interviews: Thursday 15 October 2026

About the role

This is an exciting opportunity to join a small, purpose-led organisation and play an important role in the growth and sustainability of its consultancy and training services.

Working within The Peer Partnership, a specialist peer support service, you will focus on generating new business, developing relationships with potential clients and key decision-makers, and increasing demand for The Peer Partnership's services, which include training, consultancy and service delivery.

The Peer Partnership helps organisations develop effective, safe and user-led peer support services for people living with long-term physical and mental health conditions and people with protected characteristics.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Identifying and developing new sales opportunities across the UK
- Building strong relationships with potential clients, commissioners, stakeholders and decision-makers
- Generating and converting leads for training, consultancy and service delivery
- Developing approaches to increase awareness and demand for The Peer Partnership's services
- Promoting the value and impact of peer support
- Monitoring sales and income generation activity and using results to continually improve approaches
- Supporting the ongoing growth and financial sustainability of the service

About you

You will be proactive, ambitious and creative, with experience of generating new business, sales or developing income streams.

An excellent communicator and relationship builder, you will be comfortable engaging influential stakeholders and decision-makers and turning opportunities into new business.

You will have:
- Experience in sales, income generation, business development or a related area
- A track record of developing leads and securing new business
- Strong relationship-building and communication skills
- The confidence to engage commissioners and senior stakeholders
- A commercial mindset combined with a commitment to delivering an excellent customer experience
- The ability to monitor results, identify what is working and adapt your approach
- An interest in peer support and improving outcomes for people experiencing challenging circumstances

You do not necessarily need previous charity sector experience, but you will need to share the organisation's values of respect, empowerment and inclusion.

About the organisation

You will be joining a small charity with a 30-year history of providing high-quality support services.

Its specialist peer support service, The Peer Partnership, works with people living with long-term health conditions and organisations to develop effective, safe and user-led peer support services. Through consultancy, training and service development, it shares expertise and best practice to help organisations establish and strengthen peer support.

Benefits include 26 days' holiday plus bank holidays pro rata, a 6% pension contribution, ongoing training and professional development, regular one-to-one supervision, flexible working options and a Cycle to Work scheme.

The organisation is committed to reducing inequity, valuing diversity and enabling inclusion and welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds with the appropriate skills to apply.

Other roles you may have experience of could include: Lead Generator, Sales Coordinator, Sales Executive, Income Generation Coordinator, Business Development Executive, Partnerships Coordinator, Client Development Coordinator, Sales and Partnerships Officer or Business Development Coordinator.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

title: Administrator
description: West Walk Surgery have an exciting opportunity for an Administrator to join our friendly team working up to 37.5 hours a week. We are open to fewer hours for the right candidate but they must be able to workat least Mondays and Wednesdays. Candidates should please outline your proposed working hours in your application. To apply you must be able to work to deadlines, have strong organisation skills and show attention to detail in your work. As an Administrator at West Walk Surgery you will work alongside four other Administrators helping to ensure the smooth running of the practice. Your main role will be to read, scan, code and action all documentation coming into the practice in relation to patients and in line with our set protocol for document management. As well as the above you will be responsible for undertaking a wide range of administrative duties and the provision of administrative support to West Walk Surgery patients and staff as per the job description. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administration Assistant. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Process incoming and outgoing mail. b. To read, scan, code and action all documentation coming into the Practice in relation to patients in line with the set protocol for document management. c. To arrange further appointments or tests as required (and within the postholders remit) that are specified from either the documentation or requested by the clinician. d. To report any significant events that occur in relation to document management and participate in any associated learning from incidents e. File and store records as required f. Photocopy documentation as required g. Searches/claims/recalls for QOF. h. Process changes to patient registration, deduction of record and new patient registration i. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary j. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers requests appropriately k. Always maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area l. Support all clinical staff with general administrative tasks as requested m. Help us work towards an outstanding rating with CQC

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic administrator to join our friendly, well organised, and supportive research team at our GP surgery for three days a week on a Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Hours can be agreed based on the candidates preferences, including in-school hours if desired. This post is available from now, but we are happy to wait for the right candidate. Your main role will be to provide comprehensive administrative and coordination support to the research team, ensuring smooth running of studies, effective communication with patients and staff, and accurate management of research documentation and logistics. The following are the core responsibilities of the Research Administrator. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Filing results and paperwork in participant files Keeping minutes of our research team meetings Arranging rooms for external research team visitors Maintaining Investigator Site Files and ensuring all the relevant paperwork is in the correct place Receiving and processing stock when it comes to the surgery, and arranging courier collection of samples to and from patients homes and trial laboratories Supporting the doctors, nurses and patient participants in all administrative aspects of the research study process.
